title: 1981-04-16_Pat_38.txt
concise_summary: PKD interprets his 2-74 mystical experience through Christological doctrine, arguing that Christ is formed when two psyches (an innate human psyche joined by an adventitious resurrected human psyche) combine into a single divine person. He roots this in the ditheon formula (two natures, one person) and early Christian succession, proposing that the Parousia operates through perpetual reincarnation of apostolic Christian minds returning to inhabit living humans.
key_claims: Christ is not a single entity but a 'two-nature one-person' being that can recur whenever an innate human psyche receives an adventitious resurrected human psyche
The ditheon (two-natures-one-person) formula applied to PKD's experience with Thomas means he and Thomas together constituted Christ, not that he was invaded by Christ
Thomas was an early Christian apostolic-era man (not divine) whose resurrected psyche entering PKD created the Ditheon; this differs fundamentally from simple Holy Spirit possession
The Parousia is not Christ's one-time return but a continuous process of apostolic psyches returning to inhabit new hosts, perpetuating the Kerygma unbroken from Jesus to the present

Each incarnated Christian carries forward an 'immortal man' lineage, imprinting knowledge and personality onto the next adventitious psyche, making a species-like transmission of acquired spiritual knowledge
His experience was paradigmatic: Jesus was the first Ditheon and inaugurated a new evolutionary stage of double-psyche entities with temporal dysphasic consciousness
recurring_concepts: Ditheon (two-natures, one-person): the Christological formula for a being with fully human and fully divine natures unified in one person
Adventitious psyche: a resurrected human mind/soul entering a living person from the past
Innate psyche: the original consciousness/personality of the living host
Parousia: the return/presence of Christ, reconceived as continuous reincarnation rather than single eschatological event
Logos: the divine rational principle pervading reality, conflated with Hagia Sophia (wisdom)
Kerygma: the apostolic proclamation/gospel message carried forward through the psychic lineage
Anamnesis: remembering/recollection (PKD's sense of remembering being Thomas, reconceived as psychic succession rather than literal reincarnation)
Temporal dysphasic consciousness: the two-psyche entity's ability to discriminate events through dual temporal framings
Apostolic succession: direct lineage of true Christians from Jesus through the Eleven onward, now reconceived as psychic transmission
people_entities: Philip K. Dick (PKD): the writer/visionary receiving the experience, whose innate psyche was joined by Thomas
Thomas: identified as a first-century apostolic Christian who died and whose resurrected psyche entered PKD in 2-74, creating the Ditheon
Nancy: the name of a woman in PKD's dream who receives medicine/ding and houses an adventitious male spirit, serving as paradigm for the PKD/Thomas union
Bill: character from PKD's novel BTA, conflated with Nancy, representing the innate psyche recipient
Tim Archer: character from BTA (the novel) who returns/is resurrected, paralleling Thomas's return to Bill/Nancy
Jesus Christ: the first to receive the Holy Spirit, die, and be resurrected as the inaugural Ditheon
The Eleven: Jesus's apostles who carried the Spirit after Pentecost
Father Shith: mentioned as telling PKD at St. Judes (April 1974) that the Holy Spirit enters you
Plato: classical philosopher whose Form doctrine PKD contrasts with the Stoic/Logos view
Luke: evangelist whose theological school (Antioch school, adoptionist view) PKD sees as aligned with his experience
texts_works: Encyclopedia Britannica (EB): PKD consults for the definition of 'Ditheon' and Christ's two natures
VALIS: PKD's novel trilogy referenced repeatedly; depicts the experience PKD is now reconceiving
The Bible: Acts, Pentecost narrative; adoption theme; the Paraclete/Holy Spirit
1 Corinthians 15:51-52: quoted directly ('Behold! I tell you a mystery...') on resurrection and transformation
BTA (The Broken Tarot?): PKD novel where Tim Archer returns to Bill; paradigm for his current theology
Stoic philosophy: contrasted with Platonic Forms; the Logos as immanent divine principle
Alexandrian theology: the intelligible Logos distinguished from sensible manifestation
autobiographical: 2-74 / 2-75 experience: PKD's mystical vision of February-March 1974, with which he and Thomas became a Ditheon
Seeing VALIS outside himself: PKD claims to have visually perceived an external entity (unlike the invisible Holy Spirit)
The Nancy dream: a dream in which Nancy receives medicine and a man's adventitious spirit enters her, becoming a Ditheon; PKD takes this as confirmation of his 2-74 experience
Childhood memory: the dream of little boy Philip on a raft slipping past Scotland Yard
St. Judes, April 1974: Father Shith told him the Holy Spirit enters you
Interview with Platt: PKD claims to have speculated that the mind entering him was Christ; now the dream corrects this
Rereading BTA: PKD was surprised to discover Christ's presence depicted in his own novel
Phylogenic memory: PKD sensed memories of ancestral/species consciousness, now reconceived as psychic imprinting through adventitious succession
theological_motifs: Two natures, one person (Ditheon): the orthodox Christological formula
Docetism: heresy that Jesus was wholly divine, not human
Arianism: heresy that Jesus was wholly human, not divine
Adoptionism: theology that the Holy Spirit descended on Jesus at baptism, making him God's adopted son; PKD sees his experience as confirmatory
Holy Spirit: divine presence/power entering humans; PKD distinguishes this from the adventitious psyche phenomenon
Theophany: divine appearance/manifestation; PKD notes this is 'not the full story'
Paraclete: the Spirit/Advocate sent after Jesus's resurrection; PKD conflates with the returning/resurrected psyches of apostolic Christians
Kerygma: the proclamation/message of the gospel transmitted through succession
Pentecost: initial descent of Spirit onto the Eleven; paradigm PKD uses to claim the Parousia is not limited to one person
Eucharist / Lord's Supper: the priest becomes Christ; PKD asks whether this inefficacy differs from his experience
Parousia: Christ's return/presence; PKD reconceives as continuous process, not single eschatological event
Resurrection: physical/psychic return from death; PKD argues only true Christians are resurrected into apostolic succession
Immortal man: the continuous carrier of Christ-consciousness through human history
Bride and bridegroom: mystical union; waiting for the adventitious psyche (bridegroom) to take residence (Parousia)
literary_self_ref: BTA novel: PKD notes that Bill in the Nancy dream is 'clearly bill' from BTA, and Tim Archer's return in that novel precisely depicts Thomas's return to him
VALIS trilogy: PKD asks whether his depiction of the Parousia in VALIS matches his current theological understanding; to his surprise, Christ was indeed there in BTA
The "Tears" passage: PKD references his own earlier writing and the Golden Fish sign as fitting his current interpretation
symbols_images: The raft slipping past Scotland Yard: childhood dream memory; the sensible world derived from an external agent (uttered word/logos)
The little boy Philip on the raft: PKD's innocent self before the mystical invasion
The Golden Fish sign: a disinhibiting element in the dream, releasing the adventitious psyche
Medicine/ding: the substance given in the Nancy dream that permits the union of psyches
Secret signs and passwords: used by first-century Christians in hiding from Romans; mark of Thomas's apostolic authenticity
The mystical wedding: bride (innate psyche) and bridegroom (adventitious psyche) unite
The Second Adam: Christ as restored/perfected paradigmatic human
The species metaphor: spiritual knowledge transmitted as acquired biological trait perpetuated through lineage
Temporal dysphasic consciousness: the discriminative power of the two-psyche entity experiencing time from dual positions
tensions: Anamnesis vs. Psychic succession: PKD initially interpreted his remembering as anamnesis (Platonic recollection of past lives), then rejects this as the operative mechanism in favor of psychic fusion
Invasion vs. Coalescence: Is he 'invaded' by Christ (old model) or does he and Thomas together 'constitute' Christ (new model)? This shift fundamentally changes the grammar of his theology
Reincarnation rejected yet affirmed: PKD explicitly rejects the reincarnation theory from VALIS, yet proposes a quasi-reincarnational model of resurrected psyches returning
Holy Spirit vs. Adventitious psyche: PKD struggled to distinguish between Spirit-possession and the two-psyche Ditheon phenomenon; he now claims they are distinct, but the distinction remains fuzzy
Divine equality: If each innate psyche becomes adventitious for the next host, does this mean PKD/Thomas and Jesus are equal as Ditheon? PKD admits this goes 'far beyond' normal theology

Single Christ vs. Multiple Christoses: PKD claims 'there is only one Christ' (the genre) but also that multiple Ditheons can occur; he attempts to preserve continuity through the adventitious psyche always being imprinted Jesus-ward, yet this remains internally tense
The Platt interview contradiction: PKD said in an interview that a mind entered him that 'was Christ,' but now the dream says the result of union 'is Christ,' not that he was taken over
Eucharist efficacy: PKD asks whether the priest becoming Christ in the Eucharist constitutes the same phenomenon; his answer is uncertain
evidence_quotes: "This notion that the sensible world derive from the uttered word is a strange evolution of Plato's Form doctrine."
"Christ does not enter you; the term 'Christ' refers to a 'two nature one person' being of which one nature is fully absolutely human + the other is fully/absolutely God."
"Thomas, who entered me is (or is analogous to) the man whose adventitious spirit entered nancy in the dream... Neither 'Thomas' nor I was, alone, Christ. Together we constituted Christ."

"There is, then, an unbroken personality back to it could be said to be Jesus; perhaps Jesus Each psyche imprints on the next, as making its knowledge + viewpoint available. So in this sense there is only one Christ since a 'new' one can only occur when imprinted on directly."
"This is the Parousia: it is accomplished this way. (It is not limited to one person only, as pentecost proved.)"
uncertainty_flags: The identification of Thomas as a first-century Christian is inferential; PKD notes Thomas 'seemed to be' a man and 'seemed to age' — the textual markers suggest uncertainty
The 'medicine/ding' in the Nancy dream is unclear; PKD uses a fragmentary term ('medicine/ding etc.') suggesting OCR error or unclear source
The Platt interview is referenced but not quoted in full; PKD's claim about what he said to Platt may be paraphrased rather than exact
The relationship between the Eucharist and the Parousia is posed as a question, not resolved: PKD admits 'I do not know'
The genealogical chain back to Jesus is asserted but not substantiated; how can PKD know Thomas was in direct apostolic succession?
The distinction between 'two psyches' and 'dysphasic consciousness' remains phenomenologically unclear; does the innate psyche retain autonomy during the Ditheon state?
Temporal dysphasic discrimination is claimed but never exemplified; what exactly can the two-psyche entity 'discriminate' that a single psyche cannot?
